methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - richmond.com
signals.signal_reading: Richmond.com op-ed explicitly identifies small-business AI adoption as Virginia's real challenge beyond data center infrastructure, signaling that current investments concentrate in physical infrastructure rather than distributed capability-building that would enable broad-based economic participation.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment adding 200 jobs in Henrico for AI data center infrastructure reinforces Richmond Metro as an emerging hub for AI capital deployment, but focuses on physical infrastructure rather than distributed AI fluency, concentrating technical capability in established metro corridors.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students actively helping businesses explore AI represents peer-to-peer knowledge transfer and grassroots capability building—exactly the distributed learning model that could spread deep AI fluency beyond traditional tech hubs if scaled systematically.

signals.title: Why this Virginia Tech professor says don't use AI for medical advice - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech professor's critical AI literacy work signals potential for New River Valley to become a distributed node of deep AI understanding, moving beyond surface-level adoption to develop discernment about appropriate AI use cases and limitations.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk's exploration of AI for non-emergency call handling represents shallow, platform-delivered automation that increases efficiency without building local AI capability—Hampton Roads adopting pre-packaged solutions rather than developing indigenous expertise.
